issues.problem: Per-scene tables are mis-numbered. The Mip-NeRF 360 1K per-scene table is supp. Table 10 (Deep Blending is 11, T&T is 12); Table 9 is the Ours(FastGS) runtime breakdown.
issues.evidence: source/paper.txt:831 'Table 9. Runtime breakdown ...', :884 'Table 10. Results of the 1K setting ... Mip-NeRF 360', :928 'Table 11 ... Deep Blending'. The numbers themselves (garden 27.35, counter 29.22; 3DGS 27.36/29.17; Taming 27.48/29.43) are transcribed correctly.
issues.fix: Relabel as supp. Tab. 10/11/12 in paper.md §6, paper_results.json 'source', plan.md Benchmark, bench_request 'compare' and report.md.

issues.problem: The base field is composited over white, but the official code uses black (white_background=False) for training, for the stage cache and in render_pn. The option already exists and nothing in the runtime requires white.
issues.evidence: train_lap.py: bg_color = [1,1,1] if dataset.white_background else [0,0,0], default False; render_pn.py uses the same rule.
issues.fix: Set base_background='black' for fidelity, or keep white and leave it in the gap list as now. The effect should be small on unbounded scenes.

issues.problem: This is an attribution confound, not a bug. The port follows the official LRs (opacity 0.025, shN 0.005/20 = 2.5e-4), while the gsplat baseline uses opacity 0.05 and shN 1.25e-4. A delta against baseline3dgs therefore mixes the LR change with the Laplacian mechanism. Also, the paper's method-vs-own-backbone delta is -0.13 (garden) / -0.21 (counter) dB against Taming, while the delta against the paper's 3DGS row is about -0.01 / +0.05.
issues.evidence: arguments/__init__.py opacity_lr 0.025, highfeature_lr 0.005 (/20 in training_setup); state.py rates opacities 0.05, shN 0.0025/20; paper Tab.10 Taming 27.48/29.43 vs Ours(Taming) 27.35/29.22.
issues.fix: In the report, give both paper deltas (vs 3DGS and vs Taming backbone) and name the LR difference as a confound. No code change needed.

issues.problem: Nothing checks that runtime --steps equals sum(iter_plan). With other step counts the last stage is silently truncated or runs past its LR/densify schedule.
issues.evidence: bench_request.json notes '--steps must be 30000' but the code does not enforce it.
issues.fix: Raise when the last stage's local_step exceeds plan[-1], and/or log a warning at the end if the plan was not completed.

issues.problem: The independent composition reference reuses the plugin's own P.blur and up(), so it is not fully independent. lap_pyramid does check blur/up against a numpy reference, so the combined coverage is adequate.
issues.fix: Optional: use np_reflect_conv in the composition reference.

fidelity_gaps_confirmed: Backbone: gsplat + dense Adam instead of the Taming/DashGaussian rasterizer + SparseGaussianAdam (official script --optimizer_type sparse_adam)
Archived field kept in params/GPU and cache re-rendered every step (frozen, so numerically the same cache; speed and memory claims not reproduced)
White base background vs black in the official code
Random view sampling with replacement vs the shuffled stack
Optimizer steps on the last iteration of each stage (official skips it); step-1 position LR is lr(0) not lr(1); optimizer steps before densification (official densifies first)

Verified: the Ours(Taming) rows come from run_mipnerf360_1k_taming.sh, which uses --backbone taming with PipelineParams defaults resolution_mode='const' and densify_mode='free'. So both DashGaussian schedulers are off (get_res_scale=1, get_densify_rate=1.0), and prune_and_densify_dash ignores max_screen_size (opacity-only prune). This matches the paper's description of Taming-3DGS as efficient backward + Sparse Adam.

Verified: the official loader with -r -1 (default) resizes images wider than 1600 to width 1600, which matches the w1600 dataset (PIL resize). Baseline baseline3dgs-mipnerf360-1600-30000: garden 26.934, counter 29.041.
Verified: smoke evidence shows 22.86 / 0.589 / 0.471 vs gsplat 22.95 / 0.626 / 0.439; Gaussians 207K -> 414K at the boundary (archive + full xyz inheritance)
summary: Faithful port of the official --backbone taming path. Pyramid kernel and padding, size rule, Up (bilinear + blur, same-size passthrough), signed residual rendering, clamps, training cache and eval composition, per-level targets (stage 1 supervises full-res GT through the unclamped composed image), stage-local densify/reset/SH/LR schedules, prune-first top-k ADC at rate 1, xyz-only inheritance with fresh Adam, and the official LRs and percent_dense 0.01 all match the source. 6/6 unit tests pass, and an independent GPU check confirmed signed SH colours for degrees 0-3. No critical or major issues. Minors: table numbering (10/11/12, not 9-11), white vs black base background, the LR confound in delta attribution, no steps==sum(iter_plan) guard, and one partly self-referential probe reference.
